title: A 212Gb/s PAM-4 Retimer with Integrated High-Swing Optical Driver and Chip-to-Module Long Reach Capability of 40dB in 5nm FinFET
problem: High-throughput AI/ML hyperscaler I/O interfaces require 200Gb/s+ per lane with low power budget; chip-to-module (C2M) electrical interconnects have high channel loss (~40dB) requiring equalization; eliminating external laser drivers reduces cost and form factor.
motivation: Top-of-rack switches demand higher data rates constrained by power envelopes (MSA standards like OSFP-XD); integrated laser drivers reduce external components, power, and development complexity.
method: A 4-lane 212.5Gb/s/lane PAM-4 retimer integrates high-swing laser driver directly on the TX line driver, implements 40dB C2M channel equalization via receiver-side signal processing, and operates within power/thermal budgets for AI/ML workloads.
key_novelty: Integrated high-swing optical driver on TX path eliminating external laser driver while maintaining full C2M channel equalization capability.
contributions: Integrated high-swing laser driver on line transmitter eliminating external component
40dB C2M channel equalization enabling long electrical interconnects
4-lane 212.5Gb/s/lane PAM-4 operation within hyperscaler power budget
Reduced component count and development cost for optical direct-detect systems
limitations: Specific power consumption, jitter, and BER performance metrics not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: 212Gb/s PAM-4 optical retimer with integrated laser driver and long-reach C2M equalization
